intro_html: The iconic "Swiss Pyramid" – a relentless 1700 m climb with extraordinary views of Lake Thun and the Bernese Alps. Popular funicular descent option.

routes.title_html: Mülenen → Niesen Kulm — the classic "Swiss Pyramid" ascent — A relentless but non-technical 1700 m climb from the valley floor, gaining elevation through pasture, forest, and alpine terrain. Iconic views of Lake Thun dominate the descent.
bullets_html: Reichenbach trailhead (707m) — Start point; zigzag forest trail
Stöpfflue (1105m) — First elevation pass; meet asphalt road
Schwandegg Station (1666m) — Intermediate funicular station; enters more open terrain
Niesen Kulm summit (2362m) — Restaurant and panoramic views of Lake Thun

getting_there.by_pt_html: Train + PostBus: From Thun (main station), take the regional train toward Spiez (~10 min), then board PostBus line 1 or 2 toward Mülenen (~30 min from Spiez, final stop). Combined SBB + PostBus journey ≈60 min total. From Interlaken, take the scenic train to Thun (~20 min) then proceed as above. Swiss Travel Pass covers both; check current PostBus route numbers on sbb.ch.
getting_there.by_car_html: Via Simmental: From Thun, drive south toward Spiez, then follow the scenic Simmental valley road toward Mülenen (1680m elevation, ~40 km from Thun center, ~45–50 min). Excellent parking at the Mülenen trailhead near the valley station; ample space and facilities. Alternatively, approach from Bern via Spiez. Road access is open year-round but can be busy on weekends.

day_plans.title: Day 1
rows: Depart Reichenbach trailhead; cool morning, beat crowds
Reach Stöpfflue (1105m); first viewpoint, 30 min/400m gain
Arrive Schlächtewald (1436m); steady alp road, 1 hour/330m gain
Meet Schwandegg Station (1666m); funicular line, 1 hour/230m gain
Arrive Räbmättli (~2150m); ridge approach, 1 hour/160m gain
Summit Niesen Kulm (2362m); total 5 hours up
Lunch break & summit views; restaurant open in summer
Return Reichenbach; 5+ hours down; 9.5–10.5 hours total

lapse_rate.valley_ref: Thun (428 m) — main valley reference for Thunersee region
lapse_rate.example_html: 20 °C at Thun → ~7 °C at Niesen Kulm (2362 m) — typical July afternoon. Wind exposure on the summit is high; bring extra layers.

weather.season_html: July–September is optimal: stable weather, minimal snow, warm(ish) days. June can see snow patches above 1800 m. October deteriorates with increasing cloud and wind. The Niesen-Bahn funicular operates May–October, so plan descent accordingly if using the railway.

takeaways_html: Relentless steep gain from valley floor: Unbroken 1700m ascent; no real warm-up section. Valley base (707m) is unusually low; switchbacks don't relieve grade until mid-slope.

Overwhelming funicular tourist crowds: Masses of non-hiking tourists using the train create heavy congestion on upper trails. Serious hikers avoid Schwandegg section during peak train times (1:30–2:30pm).

'Bähnli-Berg' paradox: Funicular makes it a tourist destination; lower section from Reichenbach offers escape from crowds but adds 1700m vs. using mid-station. Upper trail becomes very crowded 10:00–16:00.

gear.title: Essential
items_html:
• Hiking poles
  • Sun protection (cream + glasses + hat)
  • 2 L water
  • Emergency snacks

safety_html: Unrelenting grade: Steep ascent throughout; no terrain flattening until upper meadows. Recovery time limited; cumulative fatigue risk.
Weather exposure: Pyramid shape + 2362m elevation = exposed ridge; afternoon thunderstorms common May–September.
Trail congestion: Summer crowds peak 10:00–16:00; tight single-track on upper sections; traffic jams during turnaround.
Descent risk: Long downhill pounding on knees; loose scree on alternative descents.
Spring/winter transitions: Snowmelt creates water channels; icy sections on north-facing slopes (April, Oct–Nov).
Heat in July–Aug: South-facing slopes offer minimal shade; dehydration risk on steep sections.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
disclaimer_html: This page is an informal hike plan, not professional mountain-safety advice. Conditions change rapidly. Always check MeteoSwiss and SAC before setting out.
